routing_warnings.description: This message concerns marking a completed task done in ClickUp rather than storing its deliverable.
This message requires links to be included in deliverables rather than defining their storage destination.
The reported addition of Task 1 links belongs to the separate deliverable-link Requirement.
This message establishes the general per-task Google-folder storage workflow rather than the CRM structure artifact itself.
This message requires deliverable links generally and does not identify the CRM structure task specifically.
This message reports a blocker affecting HubSpot contact-form fields and permissions, not the Build CRM Structure deliverable.
The reported problem is the absence of a Google document or sheet for storing Pinterest Task #1 work, rather than a failure of the competitor research itself.
In context, the client's short completion statement concerns providing the missing destination for Pinterest Task #1 work.
The instruction to mark a completed task as done concerns ClickUp task-status management.
The separate statement that links were added to Task #1 concerns deliverable-link inclusion and Pinterest Task #1, not the Task #2 deliverable.
The separate statement that completed Pinterest and access-related tasks were marked complete concerns ClickUp task-status management.
This message defines later HubSpot entry for fully secured Airbnb leads rather than contact-form configuration.
The completion claim concerns setting up and populating the content bank, not scheduling or publishing posts from it.
The client's approval concerns the content-bank artifact and does not verify daily scheduling or publication.
The message establishes brand-specific content creation work rather than daily publishing from the content bank.
The instruction to list all products on TikTok Shop concerns channel publication rather than CJ product selection.
The instruction to process all 15 products changes the current batch quantity rather than product-selection criteria.
The surrounding context indicates that the reported listing error occurred on the TikTok Shop publication path.
The completion claim explicitly concerns listing 15 products on Shopify; its spreadsheet clause should be routed separately to the tracking Requirement.
The reported listing error concerns the TikTok Shop publication path rather than the daily batch-volume rule.
The update reports that eight products were listed on Shopify and is platform-specific progress, not completion of the end-to-end batch volume.
The completion claim explicitly covers listing all 15 products on Shopify, while the broader multi-platform batch remained incomplete.
The spreadsheet completion and missing-sheet observation belong to the independent product-listing tracking Requirement.
The end-of-day update confirms research and Shopify publication of 15 products but does not establish completion of the full multi-platform batch.
The client directs the freelancer to proceed with contacting Airbnb hosts but does not specify how the blocked outreach-message wording should be changed.
The message changes which leads belong in the outreach tab rather than changing the outreach-message template.
The message defines host-selection and contact workflow rather than outreach-message wording.
This message defines when a secured Airbnb lead is added to HubSpot rather than changing preliminary spreadsheet inclusion.
This message primarily establishes use of spreadsheet information for leads that become ready to schedule, rather than the scheduling behavior itself.
The final clause separately requires HubSpot entry only after the partnership has been completely secured.
The instruction to place products in women clothing and later correct their categories belongs to the separate Shopify product-categorization Requirement.
The surrounding context indicates that the listing error affected TikTok Shop, because the freelancer then proceeded with Shopify instead.
The reported Airbnb message rejection concerns the outreach template rather than host selection.
The instruction to proceed with contacting the host concerns contact execution rather than host selection.
The instruction about which interested hosts are entered into the spreadsheet concerns lead recording.
The October-to-November booking window concerns partnership scheduling after host interest.
The instruction to copy and paste the message to hosts quickly concerns contact execution.
Airbnb's rejection concerns prohibited wording in the outreach template and is best represented as a runtime failure of the message Requirement rather than duplicated under host-contact execution.

The instructions to skip reviews, choose hosts across different areas, and record only interested leads primarily refine host selection and lead-recording behavior; the command to begin contacting hosts repeats the active contact Requirement.
The copy-and-paste instruction primarily specifies use of the outreach message; its speed language is project-management guidance rather than a Requirement value.
